Meta.title: HyperSHAP: Shapley Values and Interactions for Explaining Hyperparameter Optimization
Meta.venue: The Fortieth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI-26)

research_question_1.value: How can we provide a game-theoretic explainability framework for HPO that offers local and global explanations of hyperparameters' contributions and their interactions to improve user trust and provide actionable insights?
research_question_1.reason: In the Abstract and Introduction (Section 1), the authors discuss the black-box nature of HPO undermining trust, and propose HyperSHAP to address this by explaining ablation, tunability, and optimizer behavior.

research_question_2.value: How do explanations generated by HyperSHAP compare to existing methods like fANOVA in terms of actionability for selecting subsets of hyperparameters for tuning?
research_question_2.reason: In Section 1 (Contribution 3) and Section 6.5, the authors explicitly compare HyperSHAP to fANOVA to determine which provides more actionable explanations for tuning.

hypothesis_1.value: Comparing to fANOVA, we find that HYPERSHAP's explanations are more actionable to select subsets of hyperparameters for tuning.

hypothesis_2.value: The authors hypothesise that HyperSHAP can faithfully capture and summarize higher-order interactions into interpretable explanations using Shapley values and Shapley Interaction indices.
hypothesis_2.reason: Implied in Section 1 and Section 6.2, where they aim to show that lower-order Shapley Interactions can faithfully approximate the full game behavior.

hypothesis_3.value: The authors hypothesise that the Optimizer Bias game in HyperSHAP can uncover biases and pinpoint specific hyperparameters that a black-box optimizer fails to exploit.
hypothesis_3.reason: Implied in Section 5.3 and tested in Section 6.3 by creating artificially biased optimizers to see if the framework detects the biases.

experiment_1.experiment_description: Retrieving an optimized configuration of a transformer scenario and explaining it using both the Ablation and Tunability games to compare their insights.

experiment_2.experiment_description: Investigating the interaction structure of HPO problems by measuring how well lower-order explanations approximate higher-order effects.
experiment_2.strategy: Varying explanation order and measuring Shapley-weighted loss

experiment_3.experiment_description: Creating two artificially biased optimizers (one tuning separately, one ignoring a specific hyperparameter) and evaluating them using the Optimizer Bias game.
experiment_3.strategy: Ensemble of investigated optimizer and five random search optimizers (budget = 10000 samples each)

experiment_4.experiment_description: Explaining SMAC's surrogate model throughout the optimization process at different budget milestones.

experiment_5.experiment_description: Running fANOVA and HyperSHAP (Tunability and Sensitivity) to select the top-2 important hyperparameters, then conducting a subsequent HPO run optimizing only these two.
experiment_5.strategy: Subsequent HPO run optimizing only the top-2 hyperparameters

experiment_6.experiment_description: Measuring the wall-clock runtime of HyperSHAP games across evaluated settings.

analysis_1.reason: Comparing the hyperparameter importance and interactions attributed by Ablation vs. Tunability games.

Figure 3.caption: Upset plots for Ablation (left) and Tunability (right) of lm1b_transformer (Wang et al. 2024).
Figure 3.reason: Shows the difference in importance attribution between the two games.

Section 6.1.value: HYPERSHAP's explanation shows that the majority of the performance increase is attributed to the initial learning rate (L-I)... Tunability explanation reveals that both hyperparameters, L-I and optimizer momentum (O-M), are of equal importance with a negative interaction.
Section 6.1.reason: Describes the findings from the upset plots.

analysis_2.reason: Evaluating how well lower-order Shapley interactions approximate the full game.
analysis_2.test: Comparison of R^2 values as explanation order increases

Figure 2.caption: Left: Interaction graphs showing Möbius interactions (MI), second-order Shapley interactions (SI), and Shapley values (SV)... Right: Faithfulness of lower-order explanations approximating higher-order effects...
Figure 2.reason: Demonstrates that order 3 approximates the full game well.
Figure 2.test: Comparison of R^2 values as explanation order increases

Section 6.2.value: An explanation order of 3 already approximates the full game (R2 ≈ 1) well.
Section 6.2.reason: States the quantitative result of the approximation.
Section 6.2.test: Comparison of R^2 values as explanation order increases

analysis_3.reason: Analyzing the interaction graphs of the Optimizer Bias game for the two biased optimizers.
analysis_3.test: Visual inspection of interaction graphs for non-zero effects

Figure 4.caption: Interaction graphs showing results for the Optimizer Bias game via Moebius interactions (MI) and Shapley interactions (SI) on dataset ID 3945 of lcbench.
Figure 4.reason: Visualizes the biases detected by the game.
Figure 4.test: Visual inspection of interaction graphs for non-zero effects

Section 6.3.value: The presence of both negative and positive interactions... shows that it fails to capture interactions... The blue main effect for W-D and interactions involving W-D reveal this bias...
Section 6.3.reason: Interprets the specific visual artifacts in the graphs as proof of bias.
Section 6.3.test: Visual inspection of interaction graphs for non-zero effects

analysis_4.reason: Tracking the evolution of SMAC's surrogate model beliefs over the optimization budget.
analysis_4.test: Observation of interaction graph changes over time

Figure 5.caption: Explaining the surrogate model in SMAC’s Bayesian optimization with MIs at 1%, 5%, 25%, and 100% of the budget.
Figure 5.reason: Shows the temporal evolution of the surrogate model's beliefs.
Figure 5.test: Observation of interaction graph changes over time

Section 6.4.value: Early in the process, the surrogate model exhibits numerous large higher-order interactions... By 25% of the budget, the optimizer uncovers B-S as another important hyperparameter... Eventually, as SMAC converges, the model refines its understanding...
Section 6.4.reason: Describes the changes observed in the interaction graphs.
Section 6.4.test: Observation of interaction graph changes over time

analysis_5.reason: Comparing the anytime performance of HPO runs restricted to the top-2 hyperparameters selected by fANOVA vs. HyperSHAP.
analysis_5.test: Comparison of anytime performance curves (greater than)

Figure 6.caption: Anytime performance plots of HPO runs involving only the top-2 important hyperparameters for two datasets of lcbench (Zimmer, Lindauer, and Hutter 2021).
Figure 6.reason: Shows that HyperSHAP Tunability leads to better anytime performance than fANOVA.
Figure 6.test: Comparison of anytime performance curves (greater than)

Section 6.5.value: The results in Fig. 6 confirm that the anytime performance of the runs informed by HYPERSHAP is superior to that informed by fANOVA, and that Tunability outperforms Sensitivity here.
Section 6.5.reason: Explicitly states the outcome of the comparison.
Section 6.5.test: Comparison of anytime performance curves (greater than)

analysis_6.reason: Measuring the computational overhead of running HyperSHAP.

Section 6.6.value: An Ablation game took 5s to 2m, while Tunability ranged from 6m to 15m for 7 and 4 hyperparameters, respectively... and up to 8.5h for 10 hyperparameters on the JAHS-Bench-201 benchmark.

interpretation_1.value: HYPERSHAP can reveal which hyperparameters were subject to optimization via the Ablation game, while the Tunability game emphasizes the potential contributions of hyperparameters and their interactions.
interpretation_1.reason: Authors conclude this from the difference between Ablation (showing L-I as main contributor) and Tunability (showing L-I and O-M as equally important with negative interaction) in Section 6.1.

interpretation_2.value: Thanks to the convenient properties of the SV and SIs, HYPERSHAP provides a reliable way to capture and fairly summarize higher-order interactions into more interpretable explanations.
interpretation_2.reason: Authors state this in Section 6.2 after observing that an explanation order of 3 approximates the full game well.

interpretation_3.value: HYPERSHAP can help identify such flaws [optimizer biases] and contribute to the development of more effective HPO methods.
interpretation_3.reason: Authors state this in Section 6.3 after successfully detecting the artificial biases injected into the optimizers.

interpretation_4.value: This analysis illustrates how HYPERSHAP can provide insights into the evolving dynamics of HPO processes.
interpretation_4.reason: Authors state this in Section 6.4 after tracking SMAC's surrogate model over time.

interpretation_5.value: For this specific task, the explanations from the Tunability game are more suitable [than fANOVA or Sensitivity].
interpretation_5.reason: Authors state this in Section 6.5 based on the superior anytime performance of HPO runs informed by Tunability.

interpretation_6.value: As all coalition evaluations are independent, the method is highly parallelizable, enabling substantial wall-clock reductions. Overall, this adds modest overhead to typical multi-hour HPO runs.
interpretation_6.reason: Authors state this in Section 6.6 to contextualize the runtime measurements.

conclusion_1.value: The authors conclude that HYPERSHAP is a successful post-hoc explanation framework that consistently and uniformly explains HPO across three levels (values, tunability, optimizer capabilities). They confirm that it attributes performance contributions (unlike variance-based methods), provides actionable insights for optimizing hyperparameters on related tasks (outperforming fANOVA), and effectively summarizes higher-order interactions and optimizer biases.
conclusion_1.reason: Summarized from the Conclusion section (Section 7), which ties together all the experimental findings to support the main claims and hypotheses.

suggested_research_question_1.value: How can we more efficiently approximate the max over λ ∈ Λ via simulated HPO, for example via Bayesian algorithm execution?
suggested_research_question_1.reason: The authors identify the computational bottleneck of approximating the max operator and suggest researching more efficient unbiased methods.

suggested_research_question_2.value: How can HYPERSHAP be extended to the analysis of optimizing machine learning pipelines?
suggested_research_question_2.reason: The authors explicitly state this as an important future work direction.

suggested_research_question_3.value: How can we develop HPO methods that use tunability and hyperparameter importance to learn across datasets for improving their efficiency (e.g., warm-starting HPO)?
suggested_research_question_3.reason: The authors plan to develop such methods to complement recent work on prior-guided HPO.
